text:
alexa: quick note from pairing with a customer onboarding today — we hit a weird streaming edge case in the Go generator sample app.
alexa: summary: when auth refresh occurs mid-stream and the app cancels the local ctx, the SDK sometimes emits a second partial fragment that looks like a resumed stream. New users get duplicate fragments in their stdout.
rui: can you paste the minimal repro you used?
alexa: sure, boiled down to this pattern (sample app style):

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 1500*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, &gen.Request{Prompt: "describe the long process..."})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for stream.Next() {
    tok := stream.Token()
    fmt.Printf("%s", tok) // sometimes prints replayed tokens after retry
}
if err := stream.Err(); err != nil { log.Printf("stream error: %v", err) }
```

alexa: behavior observed: token refresher triggers during active attach -> SDK performs an internal attach retry -> if app has canceled ctx (deadline hit or user cancel) we still get a few replayed tokens from the retry attach.
mike: is there any unique id or seq number with fragments? server side uses segment offsets but SDK currently doesn't expose that to client.
rui: logs from their run (timestamps truncated):

[2026-08-01T09:12:10Z] gen: attach start req=foo
[2026-08-01T09:12:11Z] auth: token near-expiry, refreshing
[2026-08-01T09:12:11Z] gen: attach retry req=foo.r1
[2026-08-01T09:12:12Z] app: ctx deadline exceeded
[2026-08-01T09:12:12Z] gen: send fragment: "initial part"
[2026-08-01T09:12:12Z] gen: send fragment: " continued" (from retry attach)

rui: thanks. That makes the race obvious. Two possible approaches: server dedupe (sequence id) OR SDK client-side dedupe.
mike: server-side dedupe would be ideal long-term (global seq per stream so reattached segments are idempotent). But short-term we need a developer-friendly fix in the SDK and the sample app.
alexa: proposal (short-term):
- change SDK: when ctx is Done, do not initiate retry-on-auth for streaming requests — return an auth error instead.
- expose a typed error for "canceled-local" vs "server-initiated-retry" so apps can handle differently.
- sample app: show pattern that buffers tokens and dedupes last N bytes based on simple overlap heuristic (helps newbies).

rui: sounds good. Also suggest a StreamOptions flag: DisableAutoRetryForStreams bool (default true for now), and add StreamMeta.Sequence uint64 in the future when server can provide it.
mike: ergonomics note: the generator stream iterator should allow an optional OnResume callback so apps can decide whether to ignore resumed content or signal to user "resuming". Something like:

```go
so := client.NewStreamOptions()
so.OnResume = func(meta gen.StreamMetadata) { /* user decides what to do */ }
stream, _ := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req, so)
```

alexa: agreed. For onboarding docs: we should update the Go sample to proactively refresh tokens before starting long-lived streams (show how to call TokenSource.EnsureFresh(ctx) or similar). Also highlight that local cancel should be preferred over relying on the server to terminate.

mike: can we add a unit/integration harness that fuzzes token expiry timings vs deadlines? I can adapt the randomized harness I use for connection tests.
rui: please do. Add deterministic seeds so CI can reproduce failures.

alexa: I'll open a small RFC PR with the recommended SDK patch (DisableAutoRetryForStreams + typed errors + sample app changes). Short-term patch will flip default to safe behavior and include migration notes.

dev-bot: alexa pushed branch fix/stream-retry-safety -> draft PR #4235
ci-bot: scheduling integration/stream-fuzz-17920 -> queued

mike: nice. One more thought: update our SDK logs to include stream correlation id on fragments so ops can trace duplicated fragments to retry attach attempts. Even if we don't have server seq yet, this will make triage easier.
rui: good call. Add that to the RFC.

alexa: created INFENG ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INFENG-2043 (includes customer repro and proposed patch).

mike: I'll pair on the harness + test. Thanks for catching this in onboarding — would have been confusing for new users.
alexa: thanks all. I'll update the sample app in the quickstart and drop a short note in the onboarding checklist.
